title: Gateway: standardize Retry-After + error shape fields for SDK classification
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Platform-facing work to make SDK retry/error handling reliable by ensuring the API gateway emits consistent headers and machine-readable error fields. This ticket is a dependency for the SDK parity initiative: clients can only respect Retry-After and classify retryable vs terminal failures if responses are consistent across endpoints and across streaming vs non-streaming paths.

Background / why:
- Support + incident learnings show SDKs diverge when:
  - 429 responses omit Retry-After or use inconsistent formats
  - error responses are missing stable error_code / request_id fields
  - streaming errors don’t include the same identifiers/shape as non-streaming
- This creates cross-language mismatches ("TS retries too aggressively" / "Go ignores Retry-After" / "Python can’t surface request_id on stream disconnect").

Scope:
1) Retry-After on rate limiting
- Ensure gateway emits Retry-After on *all* 429s that are due to rate limiting / quota enforcement.
- Accept both server-side generation and upstream propagation, but the final response to clients must be consistent.
- Format:
  - Prefer integer seconds.
  - If upstream sends HTTP-date, pass through; SDKs are expected to parse both.
- Ensure header is present for both standard JSON responses and streaming initiation failures (i.e., failing before streaming begins).

2) Error shape consistency (JSON)
- Standardize error payload fields used by SDKs and the conformance suite:
  - request_id (always present)
  - status_code (or stable equivalent in body; status code is available via HTTP but SDK conformance expects a body field when possible)
  - error_code (stable enum for classification)
  - message (safe, non-secret)
  - retryable (boolean derived from policy; used as a hint only)
- Ensure same fields exist across:
  - /v1/chat/completions (hosted)
  - /v1/embeddings
  - OpenAI-compat routes
  - streaming and non-streaming error cases where a JSON body is returned

3) Request ID propagation
- Ensure request_id is present in:
  - all error responses
  - gateway-generated errors (auth failures, rate limit, upstream timeout)
  - upstream/service-originated errors after normalization
- Ensure header + body alignment (e.g., x-request-id header matches request_id in body when both exist).

4) Security constraints
- Ensure error messages do not include API keys, Authorization headers, or environment details.
- Verify debug-mode logging (gateway) does not log secrets.

Non-goals:
- Changing retry semantics server-side beyond emitting consistent hints.
- Introducing new auth mechanisms.
- Major versioning or breaking API contract changes; these should be additive and backwards compatible.

Acceptance criteria:
- 429 responses consistently include Retry-After; conformance fixtures for 429 pass in all SDKs.
- request_id is present and stable for all errors (streaming + non-streaming).
- error_code enum is documented and stable enough for SDK classification.
- OpenAI-compat layer produces the same normalized fields (or a documented mapping) so clients don’t need per-route branching.
- Security signoff on error message safety/redaction.

Rollout plan:
- Deploy behind staged rollout (1% -> 10% -> 100%) in hosted API regions.
- Monitor:
  - 429 rate + client retry rates (risk: retry storms)
  - distribution of Retry-After values
  - error response schema validation sampling
  - request_id missing rate (target: 0)

Notes for SDK owners:
- SDKs should treat retryable as a hint; final retry policy remains per SDK standard.
- Retry-After parsing must support both seconds and HTTP-date (standard already captured in SDK PRs).
comments: 2026-02-05 (Ethan Park): Creating platform ticket per SDK parity kickoff. We need Retry-After and a stable error_code + request_id story to unblock conformance tests and reduce support churn on 429s/timeouts.

2026-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE perspective, +1. Retry-After consistency is the biggest lever to prevent thundering herd when customers set high max_attempts. Please also make sure request_id is present on gateway-generated 504/timeout errors; those are currently hard to trace.

2026-02-07 (Marcus Lin): Security review requirement: confirm error payload never includes raw auth headers; ensure any upstream error normalization redacts tokens. Prefer generic messages for auth failures ("Unauthorized") and keep details server-side only.

2026-02-10 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Implementing in gateway middleware: on 429 from rate-limit service, inject Retry-After if missing. For upstream 429s, will preserve Retry-After if present; otherwise compute from limiter window reset. Also adding schema normalization to include request_id and error_code where missing.

2026-02-13 (Allison Grant): Please add a lightweight metric: gateway_error_missing_request_id_count and gateway_429_missing_retry_after_count. We’ll use these in the rollout dashboard to ensure we’re not regressing.

2026-02-14 (Ethan Park): OpenAI-compat layer also needs normalization; otherwise SDKs see different shapes depending on route. Looping in owner via PR-433 and will ensure request_id and error_code map correctly.

2026-02-18 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): PRs up: 28411 (Retry-After on 429), 28426 (request_id propagation), 28440 (error code enum). Added unit tests + a small golden test to validate body fields. Requesting review from SRE + Security.

2026-02-20 (Marcus Lin): Reviewed. Requested one change: ensure error message for auth failures does not echo which env var/header was missing; that can lead to customers logging sensitive details. OK after tweak.

2026-02-21 (Sean Gallagher): Reviewed PR-28411/28426. Looks good. Please stage rollout and watch for retries per minute spikes in the first hour; 429 Retry-After could change client behavior quickly (in a good way, but still needs monitoring).

2026-02-24 (Connor O'Brien): Coordinating with SDK releases: platform changes should land before SDK stable rollout to avoid false negatives in conformance tests (Retry-After + error_code expectations).

2026-02-26 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Merged 28411, 28426, 28440. Deployed to canary. Metrics: 429_missing_retry_after dropped to ~0; request_id_missing in errors now 0 in canary sample. No observed retry storm; overall retry rate down slightly as clients respect longer Retry-After.

2026-02-28 (Ethan Park): Marking Done. Full rollout completed. Conformance tests in SDK repos now passing for 429/Retry-After and request_id presence. Follow-up: ensure docs reference the error_code enum and request_id troubleshooting steps (tracked in ENG-5128/ENG-5132).
